record.field: Occupation (ISCO-08)
urn:ilo:isco-08

International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO-08). A tool for organizing jobs into a clearly defined set of groups according to the tasks and duties undertaken in the job. Developed and maintained by the International Labour Organization (ILO).

Armed Forces Occupations

Occupations in this major group include all jobs held by members of the armed forces. Members of the armed forces are those personnel who are currently serving in the armed forces, including auxiliary services, whether on a voluntary or compulsory basis.
Commissioned Armed Forces Officers
Officers who hold a commission in the armed forces, including those in the army, navy, air force, and other military branches.
Non-commissioned Armed Forces Officers
Enlisted personnel who hold non-commissioned officer ranks in the armed forces.
Armed Forces Occupations, Other Ranks
Enlisted personnel who hold ranks below non-commissioned officers in the armed forces.
Managers

Managers plan, direct, coordinate and evaluate the overall activities of enterprises, governments and other organizations, or of organizational units within them, and formulate and review their policies, laws, rules and regulations.
Chief Executives, Senior Officials and Legislators

Chief executives, senior officials and legislators determine and formulate policies and plan, direct, coordinate and evaluate the overall activities of governments, enterprises, organizations and legislative bodies.
Administrative and Commercial Managers

Administrative and commercial managers plan, organize, direct, control and coordinate the financial, administrative, human resource, policy, planning, research and development, advertising, public relations, and sales and marketing activities of enterprises.
Production and Specialized Services Managers
Production and specialized services managers plan, direct, coordinate and evaluate the overall production, operations or service delivery activities of enterprises and organizations.
Hospitality, Retail and Other Services Managers
Hospitality, retail and other services managers plan, organize, direct, control and coordinate the activities of establishments that provide hospitality, retail and other services.
Professionals

Professionals increase the existing stock of knowledge; apply scientific or artistic concepts and theories; teach about the foregoing in a systematic manner; or engage in any combination of these activities. Competent performance typically requires skills at the fourth ISCO skill level.
Science and Engineering Professionals

Science and engineering professionals conduct research; improve or develop concepts, theories and operational methods; or apply scientific knowledge relating to fields such as physics, astronomy, meteorology, chemistry, geophysics, geology, biology, ecology, pharmacology, medicine, mathematics, statistics, architecture, engineering, design and technology.
Health Professionals

Health professionals conduct research; improve or develop concepts, theories and operational methods; and apply scientific knowledge relating to medicine, nursing, dentistry, veterinary medicine, pharmacy and promotion of health.
Teaching Professionals

Teaching professionals teach the theory and practice of one or more disciplines at different educational levels; conduct research; improve or develop concepts, theories and operational methods pertaining to their particular discipline; and prepare scholarly papers and books.
Business and Administration Professionals

Business and administration professionals apply concepts, principles and techniques relating to the fields of finance, management, human resources, marketing, public relations and enterprise restructuring and development.
Information and Communications Technology Professionals

Information and communications technology professionals conduct research; plan, design, write, test, provide advice and improve information technology systems, hardware, software and related concepts for specific applications.
Legal, Social and Cultural Professionals

Legal, social and cultural professionals conduct research; improve or develop concepts, theories, operational methods, software and tests; and apply knowledge related to law, social sciences, cultural industries, libraries, archives, museums, religion, arts, entertainment and sport.
Technicians and Associate Professionals

Technicians and associate professionals perform mostly technical and related tasks connected with research and the application of scientific or artistic concepts and operational methods, and government or business regulations. Competent performance typically requires skills at the third ISCO skill level.
Science and Engineering Associate Professionals
Science and engineering associate professionals perform technical tasks connected with research and operational methods in science and engineering.
Health Associate Professionals
Health associate professionals perform technical tasks and provide support services related to medicine, nursing, midwifery, dentistry, pharmacy, and promotion of health.
Business and Administration Associate Professionals

Business and administration associate professionals perform mostly technical tasks connected with the practical application of knowledge relating to financial accounting and transaction matters, mathematical calculations, human resource development, and selling and buying financial instruments and services.
Legal, Social, Cultural and Related Associate Professionals
Legal, social, cultural and related associate professionals provide technical support to professionals in legal, social and religious fields, and provide various social services to the community.
Information and Communications Technicians

Information and communications technicians provide support for the day-to-day running of computer systems, communications systems and networks, and perform technical tasks related to telecommunications and the broadcasting and recording of image and sound.
Clerical Support Workers

Clerical support workers record, organize, store, compute and retrieve information and perform a number of clerical duties in connection with money-handling operations, travel arrangements, requests for information, and appointments. Competent performance typically requires skills at the second ISCO skill level.
General and Keyboard Clerks
General and keyboard clerks record, organize, store, compute and retrieve information, and perform a number of general clerical duties.
Customer Services Clerks

Customer services clerks deal with clients and customers with respect to travel arrangements, requests for information, appointments, and operation of telephone switchboards and directory assistance services.
Numerical and Material Recording Clerks

Numerical and material recording clerks obtain, compile and compute accounting, bookkeeping, statistical, financial and other numerical data and take charge of cash register operations and of receiving, storing, issuing and dispatching money or materials.
Other Clerical Support Workers

Other clerical support workers file, copy and circulate documents; sort and distribute mail; prepare mailings; perform proof-reading tasks; encode and code data and proof-read copy; and undertake a number of clerical duties related to library operations and duties of a general clerical nature.
Service and Sales Workers

Service and sales workers provide personal and protective services related to travel, housekeeping, catering, personal care, or protection against fire and unlawful acts; or demonstrate and sell goods in wholesale or retail shops and similar establishments, as well as at stalls and markets. Competent performance typically requires skills at the second ISCO skill level.
Personal Service Workers
Personal service workers provide personal services related to travel, housekeeping, food preparation and serving, hairdressing, beauty treatment, companionship, and other personal services.
Sales Workers

Sales workers sell and demonstrate goods in wholesale or retail shops, at stalls and markets, door to door, via telephone and over the Internet. They may record and accept payment for goods and services purchased, and may operate small retail outlets.
Personal Care Workers

Personal care workers provide personal care and assistance to children in schools, residences and other settings; and provide home-based personal care and support to elderly, convalescent and disabled persons.
Protective Services Workers

Protective services workers protect individuals and property against fire and other hazards, unlawful acts and other risks. They maintain order and enforce laws, regulations and organizational or enterprise rules.
Skilled Agricultural, Forestry and Fishery Workers

Skilled agricultural, forestry and fishery workers grow and harvest field or tree and shrub crops; gather wild fruits and plants; breed, tend or hunt animals; produce a variety of animal husbandry products; cultivate, conserve and exploit forests; breed or catch fish; and cultivate or gather other forms of aquatic life. Competent performance typically requires skills at the second ISCO skill level.
Market-oriented Skilled Agricultural Workers

Market-oriented skilled agricultural workers plan, organize and perform farming operations to grow and harvest field or tree and shrub crops, and to produce a variety of animals and animal products for sale or delivery on a regular basis to wholesale buyers, marketing organizations or at markets.
Market-oriented Skilled Forestry, Fishery and Hunting Workers

Market-oriented skilled forestry, fishery and hunting workers plan, organize and perform operations to cultivate, conserve and exploit natural and plantation forests; breed or catch fish; and cultivate and gather other forms of aquatic life, or hunt and trap animals, for sale or delivery to wholesale buyers, marketing organizations or at markets.
Subsistence Farmers, Fishers, Hunters and Gatherers

Subsistence farmers, fishers, hunters and gatherers grow and harvest field or tree and shrub crops; gather wild fruits and plants; tend or hunt animals; catch fish and gather various forms of aquatic life in order to provide food, shelter and a minimum of cash income for themselves and their households.
Craft and Related Trades Workers

Craft and related trades workers apply specific technical and practical knowledge and skills to construct and maintain buildings; form metal; erect metal structures; set machine tools or make, fit, maintain and repair machinery, equipment or tools; carry out printing work; and produce or process foodstuffs, textiles, wooden, metal and other articles, including handicraft goods. Competent performance typically requires skills at the second ISCO skill level.
Building and Related Trades Workers, Excluding Electricians

Building and related trades workers, excluding electricians, construct, maintain and repair buildings and other structures; and shape, cut, fit and furnish stone, bricks, tiles, concrete and similar materials.
Metal, Machinery and Related Trades Workers

Metal, machinery and related trades workers make moulds and cores for the casting of metal; weld and cut metal parts; shape and form metal stock, cast and other metal items; erect, maintain and repair heavy metal structures, rigging, cables and related equipment; set up and set machine tools; fit, maintain, adjust and repair engines, vehicles, agricultural and industrial machinery and mechanical equipment; or make, fit, maintain and repair machinery and equipment.
Handicraft and Printing Workers

Handicraft and printing workers produce precision instruments, musical instruments, jewellery, household and other articles of precious metals, pottery, glass products and handicraft articles; perform printing work or produce printed products.
Electrical and Electronic Trades Workers

Electrical and electronic trades workers install, fit, maintain and repair electrical wiring systems and related equipment, electrical machinery, and electrical and electronic equipment used in buildings and structures and for other purposes.
Food Processing, Woodworking, Garment and Other Craft and Related Trades Workers

Food processing, woodworking, garment and other craft and related trades workers slaughter animals, and prepare the carcasses and fish for sale and further processing; bake bread and other flour products; process and preserve fruit, vegetables and related foods; tan, treat and otherwise process hides, skins and leather; make and repair shoes, bags and similar leather products; prepare tobacco and make tobacco products; perform woodworking tasks; prepare natural textile fibres and manufacture and repair a variety of garments.
Plant and Machine Operators and Assemblers

Plant and machine operators and assemblers operate and monitor industrial and agricultural machinery and equipment on the spot or by remote control; drive and operate trains, motor vehicles and mobile machinery and equipment; or assemble products from component parts according to strict specifications and procedures. Competent performance typically requires skills at the second ISCO skill level.
Stationary Plant and Machine Operators

Stationary plant and machine operators operate and monitor stationary industrial plant, machinery and equipment; or assemble products from component parts according to strict specifications and procedures.
Assemblers
Assemblers assemble component parts of industrial products according to strict specifications and procedures.
Drivers and Mobile Plant Operators

Drivers and mobile plant operators drive and operate trains, motor vehicles and mobile machinery and equipment to transport passengers and goods, move materials, dig earth, and move or lift other heavy objects.
Elementary Occupations

Elementary occupations involve the performance of simple and routine tasks which may require the use of hand-held tools and considerable physical effort. Competent performance typically requires skills at the first ISCO skill level.
Cleaners and Helpers
Cleaners and helpers perform simple tasks connected with cleaning, laundry and ironing, food and drink preparation, and running errands.
Agricultural, Forestry and Fishery Labourers

Agricultural, forestry and fishery labourers perform simple and routine tasks in the production of crops and livestock, cultivation and maintenance of gardens and parks, exploitation and conservation of forests, and conduct of fishing and hunting operations.
Labourers in Mining, Construction, Manufacturing and Transport

Labourers in mining, construction, manufacturing and transport perform simple and routine manual tasks in mining, quarrying, civil engineering and building construction, and in the manufacturing and transport industries.
Food Preparation Assistants

Food preparation assistants prepare and cook to order a small variety of pre-cooked foods and beverages and clear tables and wash dishes in fast food outlets, cafeterias and kitchens; and prepare and sell food and beverages at counters or from street stalls or carts.
Street and Related Sales and Service Workers

Street and related sales and service workers sell goods from stalls at markets or on street corners; provide various street services; and collect refuse, recover recyclable material, and sweep streets and similar places.
Refuse Workers and Other Elementary Workers

Refuse workers and other elementary workers collect refuse; recover recyclable material and perform other elementary tasks connected with keeping the environment clean; deliver and carry messages, documents and packages; and carry bags and luggage.
